item.title: Features
item.description:
• Several levels of brutality when rotating connections:

    Session pooling
    Most polite method. When a client connects, a server connection will be assigned to it for the whole duration it stays connected. When the client disconnects, the server connection will be put back into pool. This mode supports all PostgreSQL features.
    Transaction pooling
    A server connection is assigned to a client only during a transaction. When PgBouncer notices that the transaction is over, the server will be put back into the pool. This mode breaks a few session-based features of PostgreSQL. You can use it only when the application cooperates by not using features that break. See the table below for incompatible features.
    Statement pooling
    Most aggressive method. This is transaction pooling with a twist: Multi-statement transactions are disallowed. This is meant to enforce “autocommit” mode on the client, mostly targeted at PL/Proxy.

  • Low memory requirements (2 kB per connection by default). This is because PgBouncer does not need to see full packets at once.

  • It is not tied to one backend server. The destination databases can reside on different hosts.

  • Supports online reconfiguration for most settings.

  • Supports rolling restarts and upgrades using multiple processes with so_reuseport. The legacy online restart (-R) was removed in 1.26.0.

item.title: Configuration: pgbouncer.ini
item.description:
Description

The configuration file is in “ini” format. Section names are between [ and ]. Lines starting with ; or # are taken as comments and ignored. The characters ; and # are not recognized as special when they appear later in the line.

Generic settings

logfile

Specifies the log file. For daemonization (-d), either this or syslog needs to be set.

item.title: Usage: pgbouncer command
item.description:
Synopsis 

pgbouncer [-d][-v][-u user] <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer -V|-h

On Windows, the options are:

pgbouncer.exe [-v][-u user] <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer.exe -V|-h

Additional options for setting up a Windows service:

pgbouncer.exe --regservice <pgbouncer.ini>
pgbouncer.exe --unregservice <pgbouncer.ini>

Description

pgbouncer is a PostgreSQL connection pooler. Any target application can be connected to pgbouncer as if it were a PostgreSQL server, and pgbouncer will create a connection to the actual server, or it will reuse one of its existing connections.

item.title: PgBouncer compilation and installation
item.description:
Building

PgBouncer can be built with either the Autoconf-based build system or the newer, still experimental, Meson build system. Autoconf is the recommended choice for production builds and packaging for now. The Meson build is expected to become the default and the Autoconf build to be removed in a future release, so testing it and reporting any issues is very welcome. Compilation depends on a few things:

item.title: Changelog
item.description:
PgBouncer 1.26.x

2026-10-14 - PgBouncer 1.26.1 - “Only startup once”

  • Security
    • Fix CVE-2026-107350: PgBouncer 1.17.0 through 1.26.0 processed a second StartupMessage sent during SCRAM authentication when the client connected to a non-existent database. An attacker knowing the password of a user listed in auth_file could use this to log in as any other user that authenticates using SCRAM, including admins and backend superusers. This requires SCRAM authentication to be used for both users. The impersonated user can come from either auth_file or auth_query.
    • Fix CVE-2026-107349: An unauthenticated client could make PgBouncer 1.20.0 through 1.26.0 spin forever on a CPU core, and thus stop serving all clients, by sending a startup options parameter containing an empty option name such as -c=. This is only exploitable when ignore_startup_parameters is non-empty but does not contain options.
    • Fix CVE-2026-107348: An integer overflow in the packet buffer growth logic of PgBouncer 1.21.0 through 1.26.0 could cause PgBouncer to hang in an infinite loop when a client sent a packet header declaring a length above 2^31. This is only exploitable when max_packet_size is set to 2147483649 or higher, the default of 2147483647 is not affected. Since 1.23.0 this is reachable before authentication. This is the same class of bug as CVE-2026-6668, but in a different buffer implementation.
  • Fixes
    • Make ignore_startup_parameters take precedence over tracked parameters. Since 1.26.0 search_path is tracked by default, which caused ignore_startup_parameters = search_path to silently have no effect anymore. Since the release various bugs were reported around tracking of search_path parameter. These bugs will be addressed in a later release. Adding search_path to ignore_startup_parameters now restores the 1.25 behaviour of ignoring it. (bug introduced in 1.26.0)

2026-09-23 - PgBouncer 1.26.0 - “Ignore all previous search_path”

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description:
How to connect to PgBouncer?

PgBouncer acts as a Postgres server, so simply point your client to the PgBouncer port.

How to load-balance queries between several servers?

PgBouncer supports a comma-separated list of hosts in a database connection string. With load_balance_hosts=round-robin, new server connections rotate through that list. For example:

[databases]
app = host=pg1,pg2 port=5432 dbname=app load_balance_hosts=round-robin

item.title: PgBouncer 1.26.1 Documentation
item.description:
This manual is based on PgBouncer 1.26.1, released on 2026-10-14. See the release notes for the changes from earlier versions.

pgbouncer is a PostgreSQL connection pooler. Any target application can be connected to pgbouncer as if it were a PostgreSQL server, and pgbouncer will create a connection to the actual server, or it will reuse one of its existing connections.

The aim of pgbouncer is to lower the performance impact of opening new connections to PostgreSQL.
